chunks: Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things competent.

key_terms.تَبَارَكَ: Blessed is He / Exalted is He

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's absolute sovereignty and power?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often viewed as the opening declaration of Surah Al-Mulk, highlighting God's absolute dominion (Mulki) which serves as the basis for His ability to grant guidance and mercy. It underscores the theological concept that all creation is subject to His will, reinforcing the believer's reliance on divine power in both worldly affairs and the Hereafter.
